files.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: revised original match-3 duck mascot B2, tiny head / tiny feet / exaggerated abstract silhouette, three-view design sheet.
Input image 1: earlier B duck design; preserve milk white, orange bill and feet, black bead eyes, slender body and folded wings ONLY. The user now explicitly changes the PROPORTIONS toward abstraction. Input images 2-4 are actual competitor goose-in-object model renders: proportion and simplification references ONLY; study the TINY head, TINY feet, object-dominant absurd charm. Do not copy the goose's pointed bill.
Create a NEW improved white DUCK B2 as an unadorned complete standing character, in front, exact left profile, and front-left three-quarter views in three equal columns. All three must show the identical sculptural shape, same scale, same feet baseline, no text.
KEY STYLE CHANGE: exaggerated slender abstract bird, not cute baby duck, not realistic duck. Torso is a clean elongated narrow white teardrop with a tucked belly and slim flush wings, head is TINY: width about 38-42% of maximum torso width. The neck is a tapered, gently flowing extension of the chest, not a constant-radius bent tube and NOT a big round head stuck on a rod. A smooth pear-to-neck transition; medium-long curved neck, its neck/head junction barely expands. Head feels like a small soft cap at the tip of the neck rather than a separate oversized sphere. One minimal little black eye per side. The head remains distinct enough to see the tiny closed bill, but no detailed cheeks or face.
Bill: a very SMALL orange, clearly FLAT spatulate DUCK bill, compact blunt rounded tip, narrow in overall silhouette; width just 90-100% of the tiny head width, low depth and soft connection into the face. No large smiling bill, no pointed goose triangle, no protruding pancake stuck to the face.
Feet: TINY orange simplified webbed wedges, each around 18% torso width, tiny short thin legs; no broad flippers, no individually detailed toes. Abstract bold orange accents only.
Keep the overall figure very slim, elegant and slightly absurd, with the torso carrying most of its mass. Tiny subtle tail and flush wing shapes, economical rounded silhouette, no feathers, no clothes, no hair tuft, no pink cheeks, no eyebrows, no text or props. No hatchling and no doll proportions.
Neutral warm pale gray flat background, soft diffuse white studio light, smooth low-gloss toy material, broad soft shape shading, no dramatic reflections. Sophisticated simple shape design for a small mobile match-3 object; do NOT deliberately show low-poly facets or primitive sphere joints.
Composition: one horizontal three-view sheet with ample margins, fixed orthographic presentation, equal complete character heights. Prioritize a beautiful continuous sculpted silhouette while truly respecting TINY HEAD and TINY FEET.

Use case: precise-object-edit / stylized-concept.
Create one revised duck-and-object mobile match-3 toy concept.
Image 1 is the earlier fusion concept, the EDIT TARGET: preserve its prop type, dominant colour and broad design, but change the BIRD proportions to the user's new abstract style.
Image 2 is the new complete duck B2: tiny head, tiny feet, elongated slender white body, continuous sculptural neck-to-chest, small flat orange DUCK bill. Use it as the bird identity reference. The tiny head must never become an oversized cute sphere.
Image 3 is the actual competitor goose-and-prop model: use its TINY bird accents versus LARGE PROP mass as the primary proportion guide, NOT its pointed goose beak or original texture.
The PROPORTION CHANGE must be strong and immediately visible versus Image 1: the object shell occupies 85-90 percent of the visual mass. White duck body is inside the shell. Exposed tiny head is only about 10-13 percent of the shell's longest dimension; head plus bill envelope no more than 18 percent of shell length. Neck thickness 6-8 percent shell length, smoothly TAPERED, not a thick constant-radius pipe, delicate but buildable. Exposed neck can curve out of the shell, 20-30 percent shell length, no tall upright mascot standing on a costume. The head is a subtle soft widening of the neck tip rather than a separate ball.
Tiny black pin-dot eye only 5-7 percent head width, no large beads or cute doll eyes. The bill is a small FLAT blunt spatulate DUCK bill, compact, not a broad pancake, not a pointed goose triangle. Two extremely SMALL orange simplified webbed feet under/behind the shell; each foot length only 6-8 percent shell length, thin short shanks. Small white tail may barely peek out. Do not increase bird head or feet for cuteness.
Keep abstract amusing exaggeration, quiet expression, very clean simple shapes, no feathers, no hair, clothes, face decoration or accessories. The prop remains immediately recognisable. Seamless neck/face transition, not a glued on head or mouth.
One entire single assembled object in orthographic three-quarter view, camera around 25 degrees above, fully visible with generous margin. Same neutral pale gray background, diffuse white studio lighting and soft satin toy material. Broad gentle shading; no dramatic reflections, no text or labels except the existing numeral on the number-block target. This is an image concept to confirm STYLE, not a mesh render.

Specific target: EGG TART DUCK. Preserve image 1's thin shallow upright golden pastry disc with broad yellow custard face, but remove its giant duck head and huge feet. A single delicate tapered white neck and tiny head emerge near the top-right portion of the custard face; the head is close to the tart rim, not a big face above the disc. Custard remains very broad and unoccluded, the head+neck together a modest white accent on the tart face. Small flat orange duck bill. Two tiny orange foot marks beneath the disc, almost incidental. Shallow scalloped warm golden rim, a few broad toasted colour variations. It must read as EGG TART FIRST, absurd tiny duck second. No deep pastry bowl.
